newsitem.title: UK: Halifax members to vote for conversion.
newsitem.headline: Halifax members to vote for conversion.

text.p: Members of the Halifax, Britain's largest building society, meet on Monday in Sheffield and are expected to vote overwhelmingly in favour of the society's proposed 12 billion pound ($19.4 billion) flotation.
Half of the Halifax's savers must vote with three-quarters in favour of the scheme to be approved. The meeting is due to start at 1430 GMT.
Analysts said on Friday that the vote has already probably been won with postal votes from among the eight million savers and borrowers of the Halifax which has assets of over 100 billion pounds.

Each qualifying Halifax member will get a minimum of 200 shares in June if the proposal is approved. They will be worth around 1,000 pounds on the basis of an estimate made by the Halifax's advisors which analysts see as very conservative.
The flotation proposal has not been without its opponents including the Halifax Action Group which claims that borrowers and savers will be worse off once the Halifax becomes a public company.
The plan has also drawn criticism from supporters of the disabled because it pays out only to the first-named person on any account.
As a result, the elderly, disabled or children who have accounts held in trust will miss out.
A bill before parliament briefly threatened to put off the flotation but it is highly unlikely, even if the bill were to pass into law, that it would be made retrospective.

The only other building society to float on the stock exchange has been the Abbey National. Since it came to market in 1989, it has become a successful bank and has diversified away from its core mortgage lending business.
The Halifax is one of four building societies to float this year, the others being the Woolwich, the Alliance and Leicester and the Northern Rock.
